Target company: Meta Platforms (META). Meta operates Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and related social products; advertising is a major business activity. It also develops virtual and augmented reality products.

Focal announcement: Reflecting on Meta’s $8 Billion Investment in Privacy.

Decision cutoff: 2025-01-28T23:59:59-05:00. Use only information available before this cutoff.

Source: Reflecting on Meta’s $8 Billion Investment in Privacy. Published date: 2025-01-28. URL: https://about.fb.com/news/2025/01/meta-8-billion-investment-privacy.

Condensed source passage, selected from the supplied excerpt; other details are omitted: For the past few years at Meta, we’ve marked Data Privacy Day with a recap of our privacy highlights from the prior year. And they also represent the story of the more than 3,000 Meta employees and countless external experts who continue to support a world class privacy program that underlies each of our products and services and keeps people’s information safe. The privacy infrastructure we have today is due, in large part, to the landmark agreement we reached with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) in 2019. As part of that settlement, we agreed to pay a historic $5 billion fine, but even more importantly, it set us on a path to make major structural changes to our operating model and how we build products. Since 2019, we’ve invested more than $8 billion in rebuilding Meta’s privacy program and implementing sweeping changes to our data practices.
